Split and recombine a tibble with a nested column

Source: R/nested.R
split_nested.Rd

split_nested() splits a tibble with a column of nested tibbles into a parent table and a detail table that can be stored separately, e.g. as two tables in a data warehouse. recombine_nested() restores the original tibble from the two tables.

Each cell of the nested column must be a tibble with a schema shared by all cells, a zero-row tibble, or NULL.

Usage

split_nested(x, col, ptype = NULL)

recombine_nested(parent, detail = NULL, col = NULL)

Arguments

x

A tibble with a column of nested tibbles.

col

The name of the nested column, as a string or symbol. For recombine_nested(), the name of the restored nested column. Can be omitted if parent is the result of split_nested().

ptype

An optional template (a tibble, ideally zero-row) that defines the detail schema. Required if all cells of the nested column are NULL.

parent

A parent table created by split_nested(), or the split object itself.

detail

A detail table created by split_nested(). Can be omitted if parent is the split object.

Value

split_nested() returns a list of class "tibble_nested_split" with components parent and detail. recombine_nested() returns a tibble with the nested column restored.

Split layout

The parent table stores all remaining columns and, in the position of the nested column, three metadata columns:

  • .parent_id: a surrogate key that locates each parent row independently, even if all business columns are duplicated.

  • .detail_status: "rows" for a detail with at least one row, "empty" for a zero-row tibble, "null" for NULL.

  • .detail_count: the number of detail rows.

The detail table stores the columns of the nested tibbles, plus:

  • .parent_id: the parent row each detail row belongs to.

  • .row_no: the row number within its parent, used to restore the original order even if the detail table is read back in random order.

An all-empty batch (all cells NULL or zero-row tibbles) still yields a fully typed zero-row detail table, generated from the detail schema.

Recombination

recombine_nested() restores the nested column at its original position, with the original column types, duplicate details, and the distinction between zero-row and NULL cells intact. Parent rows appear in the order of the parent table, detail rows are ordered by .row_no within each parent.

Recombination is refused, naming the offending keys or row numbers, if a detail row references an unknown parent key, a row number is duplicated within a parent, expected rows are missing, or a row number is out of bounds.

Examples

orders <- tibble(
  id = 1:3,
  details = list(
    tibble(item = c("a", "b"), qty = 1:2),
    tibble(item = character(), qty = integer()),
    NULL
  )
)

split <- split_nested(orders, details)
split$parent
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>      id .parent_id .detail_status .detail_count
#>   <int>      <int> <chr>                  <int>
#> 1     1          1 rows                       2
#> 2     2          2 empty                      0
#> 3     3          3 null                       0
split$detail
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   .parent_id .row_no item    qty
#>        <int>   <int> <chr> <int>
#> 1          1       1 a         1
#> 2          1       2 b         2

# Recombination restores the original tibble,
# even if the detail table is read back in a different order
recombine_nested(split$parent, split$detail[2:1, ], col = "details")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>      id details         
#>   <int> <list>          
#> 1     1 <tibble [2 × 2]>
#> 2     2 <tibble [0 × 2]>
#> 3     3 <NULL>
